output.summary: The latest scan found 99 findings across 9 not-satisfied controls in SOC 2, ISO 42001, and EU AI Act frameworks. The largest violation groups are soc2:cc7.1 with 53 findings (vulnerability detection, largely CVEs in Django), soc2:cc6.1 with 21 findings (access control and identity), and soc2:a1.1 with 12 findings (system availability). Coverage gaps exist for 15 rules mapping to no control; 2 suppressions are applied and both expire in 2026.
output.suppressions: 2 suppressions applied: suppressions/django-cve-2023-31047 (accepted risk, expires 2026-12-27) for trivy:CVE-2023-31047 in soc2:cc7.1, and suppressions/trivy-trusted-registry (false positive, expires 2026-12-27) for trivy:KSV-0125 in soc2:cc8.1. No suppressions are expiring, expired, pending, or unused.
next_steps: Prioritize remediation of soc2:cc7.1: upgrade Django in app/requirements.txt to address 53 CVEs, starting with the 3 critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-42005, CVE-2025-64459)

Address soc2:cc6.1 security control findings: enforce non-root container execution, use a custom namespace instead of default, apply read-only root filesystem, and pin API key to environment variables
Fix soc2:a1.1 availability issues: add health checks to Dockerfile, set resource requests and limits (CPU/memory) in app/k8s/deployment.yaml

Resolve AI governance gaps: add the app/assistant component to the AI system inventory (iso42001:a.4), add disclosure that output is AI-generated (eu-ai-act:art-50), set bounded LLM calls with timeout and token limits (iso42001:a.6), and hash prompts in logs instead of logging in clear text (iso42001:a.7)
Map the 15 coverage gaps to appropriate controls or suppress them as false positives
